father.definition: a male parent; a man who raises or supports a child.
examples: My father works in a factory.

festival.definition: a special event or celebration often with music, food, and activities.
examples: We attended a music festival last weekend.

fun.definition: enjoyment or amusement; something that is entertaining.
examples: Playing games is fun.

fast.definition: moving or capable of moving quickly; also firm in belief or support.
examples: The rabbit is fast.

fry.definition: to cook in hot fat or oil.
examples: Fry the eggs quickly.
The air in the cave felt frigid.

frosty.definition: covered with frost or very cold; unfriendly in attitude.
examples: They had a frosty reception.

fork.definition: a utensil with two or more prongs used for eating or serving.
examples: She handed him a fork pretending to be fancy.

fruit.definition: the sweet and sometimes edible product of a plant; often contains seeds.
examples: We eat fruit every day.

facetious.definition: Treating serious issues with deliberately inappropriate humor.
examples: His facetious remarks during the brief were not well received.
That fella over there is a talented musician.

fire.definition: heat and light caused by burning
examples: Be careful with the fire.
The fire spread quickly.
The candles fired brightly.
The engine fired after the fuel was added.

fairness.definition: the quality of being fair and treating people equally
examples: Fairness matters in every classroom.
The decision was based on fairness.
He was furious when the car was damaged.
They became furious at the unfair decision.

forged.definition: Made in a dishonest way to look real, especially for documents or money
examples: The bank refused the forged check.
She was accused of using forged papers.

forged.definition: To create something false in order to deceive people
examples: Someone forged the signature on the contract.
They were caught after they forged documents.

fictitious.definition: Invented, not real, often used for stories or names
examples: The character has a fictitious name.
Some of the details were fictitious, not factual.

fumble.definition: To handle something clumsily, or to fail to do something because you are nervous or unprepared
examples: He fumbled the keys and dropped them.
She fumbled her speech when she forgot the first sentence.

flaky.definition: Breaking easily into small pieces; also, not reliable
examples: The paint is flaky, so we need to sand it first.
I can’t trust that flaky plan.

fetter.definition: To restrict someone’s freedom or ability to act
examples: Fear can fetter people and stop them from trying.
The rule fettered movement across the area.

fetter.definition: A chain or device used to restrain someone
examples: The prisoner wore fetters on his ankles.
They removed the fetters to free him.

feathery.definition: Like feathers; very light and soft, or looking light and delicate
examples: A feathery cloud covered the sun.
He wore a feathery scarf in winter.

foreboding.definition: A feeling that something unpleasant may happen in the future
examples: She felt foreboding about the trip.
A sense of foreboding filled the room.

foreboding.definition: Making you feel that something bad may happen
examples: There was a foreboding silence before the news.

forbear.definition: To hold back from doing something, especially out of restraint
examples: I will forbear from making any comments right now.
She forbore from arguing because she was tired.

freckle.definition: A small brown or red spot on the skin
examples: She has freckles across her nose.
The child’s cheeks are covered with freckles.

freckle.definition: To develop small brown or red spots on the skin, often from sunlight
examples: He freckles easily in summer.
The face freckled after weeks outside.

frostbite.definition: Injury to the skin and tissues caused by freezing cold
examples: Frostbite can damage fingers and toes.
He was treated quickly to prevent frostbite.

fret.definition: To worry or be annoyed repeatedly about something
examples: Stop fretting and focus on what you can control.
She fretted about the missing files all morning.

framework.definition: A basic structure that supports something or gives it organization
examples: The framework makes it easier to organize the code.
They built a framework for the report.

flicker.definition: to shine or move quickly in an irregular way
examples: The candle flickered in the wind.
The screen flickered and then went black.

flicker.definition: a brief irregular change in light or movement
examples: I saw a flicker of light behind the curtain.
There was a flicker in the signal.

forbid.definition: to officially or strongly tell someone not to do something
examples: The rules forbid smoking indoors.
They forbade him to return.

float.definition: to stay on or move through a liquid or air without sinking
examples: The leaf floated on the water.
Helium balloons float in the air.
The smell of food floated through the hallway.
His voice floated across the room.

float.definition: a thing that floats, or a buoyant device
examples: The fishing net uses a float to keep it on the surface.

foggy.definition: covered with fog or making it hard to see
examples: It was foggy in the morning.
The instructions were foggy to me.

fondness.definition: a strong liking or love for someone or something
examples: She has a fondness for old books.
His fondness for tea surprises me.

forensic.definition: related to using scientific methods to investigate crimes or legal issues
examples: The forensic team collected fingerprints.
Forensic evidence helped solve the case.

finicky.definition: careful about details and easily dissatisfied
examples: He is finicky about spelling.
The chef is finicky with ingredients.

fussy.definition: careful and easily worried about small details or cleanliness
examples: Stop being fussy and help me carry it.
She’s fussy about her clothes.

fraud.definition: dishonest behavior meant to trick people for money or advantage
examples: The company was accused of fraud.
It was a fraud to take your bank details.

fraud.definition: to commit fraud or trick people dishonestly
examples: He frauded customers by selling fake tickets.
They frauded investors with false reports.

foreordain.definition: to decide that something will happen in advance
examples: They believed the outcome was foreordained.
The event was seen as foreordained.

farseeing.definition: thinking about the future and planning wisely
examples: Her farseeing decisions helped the company grow.
A farseeing leader prepares for risks.

features.definition: distinct parts or characteristics of something, especially a face
examples: Her facial features are very distinctive.
The software includes helpful features.

frosted.definition: covered with a thin layer that looks like ice or with a cloudy surface
examples: The windows are frosted for privacy.
She bought a frosted glass bowl.

frizz.definition: hair that becomes rough or forms small irregular curls, often in humid weather
examples: She hates frizz during rainy days.
The frizz made her hair look messy.

frizz.definition: to become rough and irregular, often because of moisture or lack of moisture
examples: My hair frizzes in humidity.
The fibers begin to frizz after washing.
